ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Cars A and B travel on a straight and level lane. Their v–t graphs of motion are shown in the figure, in which A's graph is two identical arcs, and B's graph is a straight line, then which of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: According to the v-t graph in the figure, must cars A and B meet at t=4 s?

matched_variant_raw.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
matched_variant_raw.rewritten_question_text: According to the v-t graph in the figure, must cars A and B meet at t=4 s?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to the v-t graph in the figure, must cars A and B meet at t=4 s?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: The figure is a v-t graph, with the horizontal axis as t/s and the vertical axis as v/(m·s^-1). A's velocity graph starts from near t=0, v=0, gradually increases with time, and is about 2 m/s at t=4 s, with a shape of two identical arcs; B's velocity graph is a straight line decreasing from t=0, v=2 m/s to t=4 s, v=0. The two graphs intersect at about t=2 s, v=1 m/s. Then reason: the area under a v-t graph represents displacement, but to judge whether the two cars meet at t=4 s, it is necessary to compare their actual positions at t=4 s. It can be written as x_A(4)-x_B(4)=[x_A(0)-x_B(0)]+∫0^4[v_A(t)-v_B(t)]dt. The graph can at most give the displacements or displacement difference of the two cars from 0 to 4 s, and cannot give the initial position difference x_A(0)-x_B(0) of the two cars. The problem statement only says that the two cars move on the same straight line, and does not state the initial positions. Therefore, even if from the areas it is judged that the two cars have the same displacement from 0 to 4 s or the displacement difference can be found, it still cannot guarantee that the position difference at t=4 s is 0.
